control.name: CONTROL — disarm the width bound entirely (every width is admissible)

mutations.name: off-by-one the ceiling (a width EQUAL to the maximum is refused) — the desk's own `--width 8` on the review pool would be rejected, and a bound that refuses the case it was built for is one operators route around
delete the BUDGET arm — a width would then be bounded only by the number a human wrote in the table, with nothing tying it to the writes the role actually makes
delete the TOKEN arm — the review pool's ceiling would stop tracking the shared App token's secondary-rate-limit trip, which is the entire reason it is narrower than the worker pool
take the MAXIMUM of the arms instead of the minimum — every ceiling would be satisfied by the loosest one, which is the opposite of a conjunctive bound
let a bad token-concurrency override fall back to the shipped default — a deployment declaring a NARROWER ceiling would silently run the wider one
widen THROUGH an open circuit breaker — adding agents multiplies exactly the non-progress that opened it
drop the READ-time ceiling clamp — a width stored before a budget constant was lowered would outlive the bound that admitted it
never expire a stored width — a coordinator that died would leave a pool permanently wide, with no live session that knows why
treat a corrupt width entry as 'no width set' — a width the desk is relying on would silently revert while every instrument reported the default as deliberate
mutations.old: return nil, false, Unverifiable("malformed width entry at "+path+
mutations.new: return nil, false, nil // was: Unverifiable("malformed width entry at "+path+

mutations.name: snapshot the pool cap instead of re-reading it per pass — the whole point of the knob: a width set between ticks would never reach the loop
let an unreadable width widen the pool — ignorance about a pool's size would grow it rather than hold it at the configured floor
